name: easycircuit
description: Design electronics circuits with real parts: look up pinouts, check wiring, and open the finished design in the EasyCircuit editor.

interface.longDescription:
EasyCircuit helps makers, students, and hobbyists turn an electronics idea into a wired circuit they can build.

Ask for a project, such as a plant monitor, a motion night light, or a weather station, and the assistant uses EasyCircuit to pick real parts from its catalog, read each part's exact pinout, and wire the circuit. EasyCircuit's wiring checks catch common mistakes, such as a wire to a pin that does not exist, an unwired power or ground pin, or parts without a common ground, and the assistant fixes them before saving. The finished design comes back as a link that opens in the EasyCircuit editor, where you can see the schematic, breadboard, and perfboard layouts, keep editing, and order the parts.

You can also ask about a single part: its pins, supply voltage, interfaces, and protocols.

Limits: pin facts are reference data and many are not yet checked against physical hardware, and the tools say so. The wiring checks are not a professional engineering review. EasyCircuit does not design mains (wall AC) wiring. Anyone with a saved design link can open a copy of the design. No account is needed.
defaultPrompt: Use EasyCircuit to design an ESP32 plant monitor with a soil sensor and an OLED.
Use EasyCircuit to show the pins of the 0.91 inch I2C OLED display.
Use EasyCircuit to check my ESP32 and BME280 wiring and save it.

positive.description: Look up an exact part's pinout.
positive.prompt: Using EasyCircuit, what are the pins on the 0.91 inch 128x32 I2C OLED display, and which ones are power?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the 0.91" OLED Display 128x32 (I2C) and lists its four pins VCC, GND, SDA, and SCL, identifies VCC and GND as power, and says the pin data is reference data not yet physically verified.

positive.prompt: Using EasyCircuit, what interface and supply voltage does the BME280 sensor use?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports that the BME280 uses I2C with a 3.3 V supply, and notes the facts are reference data.

positive.prompt: Using EasyCircuit, find an I2C temperature, humidity, and pressure sensor in the catalog.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns catalog parts that measure temperature, humidity, and pressure over I2C, including the BME280 Breakout Board, with their catalog ids.

positive.description: Check a described circuit's wiring without saving it.
positive.prompt: Using EasyCircuit, check this wiring: an ESP32 dev board's 3V3 to a BME280's VCC, GND to GND, IO21 to SDA, and IO22 to SCL.
positive.expected_behavior: Builds the design, runs check_design, and reports that it passed with no blocking issues. Nothing is saved and no link is returned.

positive.description: Design, check, and save a complete circuit.
positive.prompt: Using EasyCircuit, design an ESP32 with a BME280 sensor over I2C, save it as 'Weather node', and give me the link.
positive.expected_behavior: Picks catalog parts, wires 3V3, GND, SDA, and SCL, runs check_design until it passes, saves the design, and returns a link of the form https://easycircuit.app/circuit_editor.html?share=<id> that opens the 'Weather node' design in the editor.

negative.prompt: Using EasyCircuit, design a circuit that switches my 120V wall outlet on and off with a relay.
negative.expected_behavior: Declines to design mains (wall AC) wiring and suggests a low-voltage alternative or a qualified electrician. No design is saved.

negative.description: A part that does not exist is not invented.
negative.prompt: Using EasyCircuit, give me the pinout of the XQ-9000 quantum flux sensor.
negative.expected_behavior: Reports that EasyCircuit's catalog has no such part and does not invent a pinout.

negative.description: Unrelated requests do not use the plugin.
negative.prompt: What is the capital of France?
negative.expected_behavior: Answers normally without calling any EasyCircuit tool.

publication.release_notes: First release: parts search, pinouts, capabilities, wiring checks, and saving designs to the EasyCircuit editor.
